bullets.title: Oil -5% on Iran-US Hormuz MOU reports; White House denies, but oil/energy lags
bullets.body: Iran's state TV reported a draft MOU framework with the US including military withdrawal and naval blockade lifting, triggering Brent crude to fall more than 5% intraday to ~$89.41, the lowest level since April 20. The White House denied Iranian media claims and Rubio made de-escalation comments, but the move drove airlines (+3.5%), housing (+2.4%), and consumer discretionary (+1.6%) sharply outperforming while energy and oil services lagged.

bullets.title: S&P 500 flat on the day with 19 YTD all-time highs; JPM tactically bullish
bullets.body: S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended near flat/record closes as AI momentum trade took a breather following recent rallies. JPM remains tactically bullish, citing robust tech fundamentals and consumer strength; historical precedent with 19 ATHs through May implies 50+ for the full year. Global hedge fund net momentum exposure sits at historical highs with Tech the most-bought sector last week.

bullets.title: Core PCE expected +3.3% y/y tomorrow; Fed's Kashkari turns hawkish, Cook warns on AI inflation
bullets.body: April core PCE deflator is expected +0.25% m/m, lifting the y/y pace to ~3.3%, the highest since 2023. Fed Governor Cook warned that the $1.5T+ AI infrastructure boom could drive inflation via semiconductors, energy, and construction labor. Separately, Fed's Kashkari flagged that inflation risks outweigh labor market risks and said the Fed could embark on a series of hikes if Middle East-related inflation materializes.

bullets.title: 7-year Treasury auction tomorrow looks rich; 5-year cleared in-line for first time since Oct 2025
bullets.body: JPM views the 7-year sector as significantly rich after controlling for Fed expectations, inflation, and growth, expecting more concession needed at tomorrow's $44bn auction. 7-year yields are up 14bp since the prior auction but down 20bp from mid-May peaks; foreign takedown at the last auction dropped 5.4 pts to 10.5%. Today's 5-year auction cleared in-line—first time without a tail since October 2025. 30-year bond resistance expected at 4.90.

bullets.title: ADP private payrolls 4-week avg slides to 35.75K from 42.25K; Richmond Fed surges to +13
bullets.body: ADP weekly private payroll 4-week average dropped to 35.75K from 42.25K prior, signaling labor market moderation. Offsetting that, the Richmond Fed manufacturing index printed +13 vs. +2 consensus, with notable improvement in new orders and shipments—mixed macro signal heading into Friday's PCE.

bullets.title: Semis -1.4% as overbought conditions and ZS whipout pressured the AI-momentum sub-sector
bullets.body: Semiconductors were the weakest S&P sector on the day despite strong individual prints, as overbought conditions and supply pressure weighed. ZS plunged 31.5% (largest daily drawdown ever) after unchanged FY26 ARR guidance, lower FCF, and disappointing FY27 outlook; the move raised the bar for all high-flying software/security names. TSM (+2.5%) and MU (+3.6%) were exceptions, with MU briefly breaching a $1T market cap.

bullets.title: MRVL beats with exceptional AI bookings; raises FY27-28 guidance significantly
bullets.body: Marvell Q1 revenue $2.42B (+28% y/y) came in just above consensus, but the guide was the story: Q2 guided at $2.70B (+35% y/y) well above the $2.60B estimate, and management significantly raised FY27 and FY28 revenue outlooks—FY28 now seen around $16.5B—driven by exceptional AI-related bookings across 800G/1.6T optics, 51.2T Ethernet switches, and custom XPU solutions. Revenue expected to accelerate each quarter through FY27.

bullets.title: SNOW +32% AH: product revenue re-accelerates +34% y/y; FY27 guide raised $180M; $6B AWS deal
bullets.body: Snowflake F1Q product revenue of $1.334B (+34% y/y) beat consensus by $66M, marking the strongest sequential dollar growth ever and the highest beat since F3Q25. F2Q guide of $1.415-1.42B (30% y/y) beats the 26% consensus estimate; FY27 product revenue guide raised to $5.84B (+31% y/y). The company announced a $6B multi-year AWS partnership and acquired Natoma (enterprise MCP platform). NRR improved to 126%; 46 new $1M+ ARR customers added in Q1 vs. 26 prior year.

bullets.title: CRM beats on EPS ($3.88 vs $3.13 est) and raises FY EPS guide; Agentforce ARR reaches $1.2B
bullets.body: Salesforce Q1 EPS of $3.88 beat the $3.13 FactSet consensus by 24%, with revenue of $11.13B slightly above. FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $14.06-14.12 from $13.11-13.19 prior. Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B (from $800M last quarter) with 3.8B AWUs. Q2 revenue guide of $11.27-11.35B came in at the low end of consensus. FCF and billings were slight misses vs. expectations, and management guided 2H acceleration.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex analysis: AWS/GCP growth estimates may be conservative; MS raises GOOGL bull case to $460
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates hyperscalers will add ~14GW in 2026 and ~20GW in 2027; current AWS/Google Cloud growth forecasts of ~36%/86% in 2027 imply $11-14B incremental revenue per GW, suggesting estimates could be conservative. Google Cloud's $11B per GW of implied incremental revenue offers the most upside. MS raised its GOOGL bull case from $425 to $460 (28x 2027 bull-case EPS of ~$16.50). Industry capacity deals are reportedly being negotiated at $20B+ revenue per GW.

bullets.title: META +3.7% on subscription launch: Instagram/Facebook at $3.99/mo, WhatsApp at $2.99/mo
bullets.body: Meta announced paid subscription tiers for Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp with AI-focused plans coming. Bulls view this as fully incremental revenue against rising AI cost pressures. The stock gained 3.7% on the day.

bullets.title: HOOD launches agentic trading: AI agents can trade stocks and make credit-card purchases autonomously
bullets.body: Robinhood announced a platform feature allowing customers to delegate investing and credit-card spending to AI agents such as Anthropic's Claude or Cursor. The feature is planned to expand to derivatives, crypto, and prediction markets. Cards/Payments/Fintech sector was up 0.1% on the day while broader S&P Banks fell 1.8%.

bullets.title: Retail investor share of US equity trading hit 4-year low of 17% in Q1; call buying surging in April-May
bullets.body: JP Morgan notes retail's share of US equity trading fell to 17% in Q1 2026, near post-pandemic lows, but call option buying by small traders has risen sharply in April-May after subduing Oct 2025-Mar 2026. Foreign equity purchases in the US fell to ~$10B/month in Q1 from ~$80B/month in H2 2025, though Korea and Taiwan current account surpluses ($240B and $270B projected for 2026) offset GCC surplus collapse. Bitcoin and gold ETFs both saw outflows in the past two weeks.

bullets.title: Data center power/energy access the limiting factor for HPC growth; Jefferies sees data center load accelerating
bullets.body: Hyperscale data center providers are outperforming traditional REIT incumbents as investors place a premium on de-risked energy access amid NIMBYism. Jefferies notes PPL with ~10GW under ESAs and DUK raised to 7.6GW from 4.5GW in data center commitments. Microsoft signed a 140MW solar PPA with Avangrid (combined contracts now exceeding 500MW). OKLO received a Goldman PT raise to $66 on a DOE plutonium conversion program selection.

bullets.title: TSM raising 3nm prices up to 15% in H2 2026; data point on AI chip pricing power
bullets.body: Taiwan Semiconductor is raising prices on its 3nm process node by up to 15% in the second half of 2026. The move underscores sustained AI-driven demand and pricing power at the leading-edge node level.

bullets.title: Software earnings bar now higher after ZS miss and NET inline print; market demands AI revenue acceleration
bullets.body: The GS TMT desk notes NET and ZS prints have raised the bar for high-flying software and security names heading into earnings, with the market seeking clear evidence of AI revenue acceleration—not just bookings or ARR growth. ZS was downgraded to in-line at Evercore ISI with a PT cut to $155 from $225. The security software sub-sector bore the brunt of the selloff.

bullets.title: SNPS beats Q2 and raises FY26 EPS guide to $14.72-14.80; Elliott's Jesse Cohn joins board
bullets.body: Synopsys Q2 EPS of $3.35 beat the $3.15 consensus; FY26 EPS guidance raised to $14.72-14.80 from $14.38-14.46, ~$0.30 above prior midpoint. FY26 revenue guidance raised to $9.625-9.705B; FCF guidance raised to ~$2B from ~$1.9B. Elliott Investment Management (multi-billion dollar stake) appointed Jesse Cohn as independent director effective June 1, pushing for margins to match rival Cadence; company entered a cooperation agreement with customary standstill.

bullets.title: Bytedance capex stepping up to $70B in 2026 and $100B in 2027; VNET captures 510 of 517 MW won YTD
bullets.body: Goldman reports Bytedance is weighing $70B in capex this year and $100B next year (up from $25B in 2025) for its AI push. VNET secured 510 MW of 517 MW YTD order wins from Bytedance, positioning it as the primary beneficiary of the step-up. GDS faces headwinds from slower pacing shown in Q1 and contract renewals at potentially worse terms.

bullets.title: S&P index changes effective 1-Jun-26: FDXF added to S&P 500; EPAM exits to small-cap 600
bullets.body: FedEx Freight (FDXF) will be added to the S&P 500 effective June 1 following its spinoff from FDX, which remains in the S&P 500 and 100. EPAM Systems exits the S&P 500 and replaces Shutterstock in the S&P Small Cap 600; SSTK is expected to be acquired soon. Dave (DAVE) replaces American Woodmark (AMWD) in the Small Cap 600.

bullets.title: Goldman warns pension selling could intensify month-end amid weakening liquidity and mega IPO pipeline
bullets.body: Goldman flagged that pension-selling pressure could accelerate into month-end against a backdrop of weakening market liquidity and a looming mega IPO pipeline, presenting a near-term technical headwind for equities.
